gen-gf-warnes-gf-changa: Warnes draws ink strokes that taper out before touching, stretched wide like glass tubing bent into letters. Changa does the opposite job, with a lowercase that stands as tall and solid as cast iron capitals.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-days-one: Wire-bent sign energy, stretched out wide and spacious, is what Warnes brings. Days One fills the line with a towering x-height, giving those constant-width strokes something solid to lean against.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-epunda-sans: Warnes writes with a ballpoint's pressure-free line, stretched wide and a bit theatrical. Epunda Sans is the quieter worker, with oversized e and a counters that let daylight into every curve.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-mitr: Mitr packs almost no gap between x-height and cap height, which makes it feel compact. Mitr then sits under the pipe-cleaner letterforms of Warnes, stretched and spacious, as the dense counterweight.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-viga: Viga reads solid and uniform, its capitals barely taller than the lowercase. Shrink Warnes down and its stretched, tapering ink strokes lose their drama, so it wants room to spread beside that sturdy body.
gen-irish-grover-gf-aclonica: Tall lowercase makes every word in Irish Grover look sturdy and large, with softly varied strokes. Aclonica stretches out beside it, widely spaced letters with a deep midsection and a thickness shift you feel more than see.
gen-irish-grover-gf-allerta: Heavy verticals pull faintly against lighter horizontals in Irish Grover, all in sturdy tall letters. And Allerta, wide and loosely tracked, can stay modest in size, since its prominent x-height already carries the line.
gen-irish-grover-gf-alumni-sans-pinstrip: Irish Grover moves with a soft rhythm of heavier and lighter strokes, its tall lowercase looking sturdy and large. Alumni Sans Pinstripe holds a single line weight, tight and compact.
gen-irish-grover-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Alumni Sans SC squeezes its letters close, with a lowercase that looks oversized beside its own capitals. But Irish Grover brings the loudest note, tall open-throated lowercase that makes words look sturdy.
gen-irish-grover-gf-anaheim: Anaheim packs rounded, open-sided forms into a dense huddle the eye slides through. But Irish Grover keeps a visible yet restrained stroke contrast, so Anaheim is the one to nudge up in size.
